speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your symptoms, could you describe the nature of your chest pain and when it started relative to the vomiting? Also, have you experienced any fever or recent travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture)

I suspect you have suffered a tear in your esophagus due to the forceful vomiting; this is a life-threatening emergency. We need to confirm this immediately with a contrast esophagogram or CT scan of your chest. Please stay still while we prepare these urgent images.
